#3868. EA really doesn't want you to delete Madden NFL 27 to make room for GTA 6

"Don't let 210GB get between you and your league."

Assuming you didn't just buy a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S to play Grand Theft Auto 6, your console's limited storage space is likely already strained, meaning tough choices may have to be made to make room for Rockstar's chonky 212GB crime game.

In a move I don't remember seeing before, EA is asking players to spare Madden NFL 27 from the purge to free up console storage space. As spotted by Push Square, a desperate in-game message pops up when you launch the American Football game, pleading with you not to delete it.

The message highlights 17th November as the date of a Madden NFL 27 update, though its styling, wording and choice of background seem to hint at GTA 6.

"Don't delete!" it reads, as shared by Zirksee on X. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17… do not leak this transmission."

EA's language and intention, however, are much clearer in this post on X, which specifically references GTA 6's large file size in a cheeky way, seemingly promoting the same update.

"Don't let 210GB get between you and your league," the post reads, clearly quoting GTA 6's file size.

The update in question is fairly notable, adding a Madden 97 throwback with era-appropriate players, playbooks and what looks to be 16-bit visuals. Though it's obviously not related to GTA 6 in any way, it's easy to see why EA would fear a significant drop in players once Rockstar's game arrives, something other publishers are undoubtedly worried about.

As part of a recent restructuring, EA laid off 400 employees, closed down BioWare, cancelled unannounced projects and revealed a refocusing on its core franchises and biggest monkey-makers. That includes EA Sports, of course, where a team is currently developing a game codenamed Project Gridiron, described as "a social-first open-world experience for our American Football team".

#3867. GTA 6 Comparison Reveals Two Advantages Of Xbox Series X Over PS5

The good folks over at Digital Foundry are still busy analysing all things to do with GTA 6's launch last week, and their latest comparison takes a look at all four console versions alongside each other - Series X, S, PS5 and PS5 Pro.

They also go on to rank the versions in order, and perhaps surprisingly, Xbox Series X comes out on top versus the standard PS5. Two reasons are given for this, which are that the Xbox version supports 120Hz VRR to smooth out the dips in frame rate, and that the PS5 sometimes "suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X".

"Although both target 30fps and maintain it during typical gameplay, heavy vehicle traversal and intense airport crowd sequences cause frame-rates to drop into the mid to upper 20s. PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips. Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off."

Visually, there are said to be no real differences between the Xbox Series X and PS5 versions, although the Series X version does have "slightly more pronounced heat haze effects in one opening shot".

All of this is obviously beaten by the PS5 Pro though, which is said to "deliver the definitive console GTA 6 experience by leveraging its larger GPU, accelerated machine learning hardware and enhanced ray tracing features".

"Overall, the PS5 Pro leads the rankings with its superior visual detail and rock-solid 30fps target, followed by the Xbox Series X - which edges out the standard PS5 through better performance stability. The Xbox Series S sits at the bottom due to visual trade-offs, unstable frame-rates and audio glitches."

It's fair to say we never expected the Xbox Series X version to fare better than the PS5 version in this case, especially considering all the "plays best on PS5" marketing that surrounded GTA 6 prior to release.

Of course, Digital Foundry seeks out the most minute of details when it comes to technical analysis, and the differences between the Xbox Series X and standard PS5 versions aren't going to be major enough to suggest one version is far better than another. It's just interesting that they've ended up ranking the Series X higher in this instance.

Let us hear your thoughts in the comments, but please do keep it respectful! We enjoy the PS5 as well, and know plenty of people who are loving the game on that system. All the same, this is a fascinating analysis and a bonus for Xbox.

#3866. World of Warcraft: Forever's in-game economy has been ravaged by an exploit that allowed players to farm thousands of gold

World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.

This exploit was quickly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a currently-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits. In basic terms, the new Blackmaw Hold dungeon includes several packs of non-elite, easy to kill enemies right at the start of the dungeon. Prior to the hotfix, the loot drop tables for these enemies were incorrect, and worth vastly more in terms of gold than they should have. Keen-eyed players spotted this but kept it quiet, running into the dungeon and quickly killing off these early mobs and resetting the dungeon every hour.

This was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours. He is seen streaming with over 4,000 gold - and claims other streamers made out with more than that.

For an idea of how much money that is, one of the most expensive things a player will likely buy on their character throughout the original Classic World of Warcraft is the expert riding skill. It takes a long time to save up for, and stands as a major accomplishment in the life of a character. It costs around 900 gold. These players, in just a few days of dedicated grinding, will have been able to pay this price several times over.

Looking at community hubs for the game (Reddit or the official World of Warcraft forums), regular players are demanding Blizzard take action - going further than just the already-deployed hotfix. Maya on the WoW forum wants the ill-gotten gold to be removed and for players to be banned who made use of the Blackmaw Hold exploit, writing: "Remove the gold or I and many others will just quit. This is worse than the bots at this point."

Flnrodi on Reddit, referring to streamers who took advantage of this exploit, wrote: "Not sure what to say. The fact that he did this all offstream says enough that [Ziqo] (and others) knew that this is not intended and 100 percent considered an exploit. Personally, I think there should be some kind of punishment and definitely all the gold [should be] revoked."

You may be wondering why this is such a big deal? So what if a few players can get fancy mounts faster, or snatch up some really good gear on the player auction house? Well, exorbitant sums of money in the hands of a few players can have a massive impact on a server's economy. You could, for example, use your newfound wealth to flip every listing of a certain rare resource on the auction house and mark the price up significantly for profit, which obviously inflates the price for regular players. Likewise, you can out-bid other players for rare and powerful BOE items, which in turn raises the prices of those as sellers may find they can make more cash than they could off such drops prior to the exploit.

This all has an inflationary effect, and could push a server's economy to a more expensive level faster than it otherwise would. Even if this effect isn't so drastic, these players can essentially gear out multiple characters in fantastic gear without putting in the hours, or out-bid the rest of the community on the Black Market Auction House for rare and largely unparalleled special loot.

The counter argument against punitive measures is that these players didn't cheat. They didn't buy gold from real-money-traders, nor did they plug in some external tool to give them an unfair advantage over others. They simply put in the time to get to around level 55, ran a dungeon, and killed mobs repeatedly for valuable drops. Would it have been a good thing to flag the exploit the moment they found out about it? Sure. But once other players at your level take advantage of it, and no strict ruling around whether doing so is punishable, it's arguably in a player's best interest to join in while the going is good.

As of writing, there's been no official word from Blizzard on what it intends to do beyond fixing the exploit. Given the required level to take on Blackmaw Hold, the number of exploiters cannot be too large, and the sheer amount of gold they gained in a small amount of time should make them easy to flag. Rolling back their accounts and reverting the gold they gained back to a pre-exploit amount certainly appears to be a popular option. Whether Blizzard actually does so, or enforces other punishments, is the big question.

#3865. Former Dishonored designer joins the team on New Blood's Victorian immersive sim Gloomwood, with a new level and new weapons coming this year

Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest update post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.

In addition to his work at Arkane on Dishonored and its sequel, Deathloop, and even Marvel's Blade, Eveillé also developed his own indie horror, 2024's short and sweet Threshold. It's quite a legacy to add to this team, and his hiring is described by New Blood as an example of how "finding level designers who are up to the task of working on Gloomwood is not easy". The post also mentions that Eveillé will be added alongside "our new devs", implying that he's not the only new addition to the team.

Other than these new hires, the update is set to include quite a bit to change up Gloomwood and make it bigger. The highlight is the First National Bank level, which is described as "our largest and most intricately designed level yet", with the screenshots showing off a grand and imposing, yet claustrophobic in places, that makes the act of going to the bank even more intimidating than usual. The Bank is joined by the new stun prod weapon, which is self-explanatory, and the new Rat and Fishdog transformations, which let you sneak through crawlspaces and swim through dirtied waters respectively. That sneaking will be made more difficult by the addition of alarms and blood pools that both alert surrounding guards to your presence, though the new Crow King transformation offers a new, acid-belching way to take down any guards that come running.

The update is tentatively scheduled for "before the end of the year", but New Blood aren't setting down a specific release date. Rogers himself will also be going through back surgery very soon, for which I wish him a gentle recovery and, hopefully, as easy a return to work as possible.

#3864. God of War Laufey Star Will Reprise Role for Live-Action TV Show

God of War Laufey’s lead Deborah Ann Woll will reprise her role as Kratos’ wife Faye in Amazon Prime’s upcoming live-action TV adaptation.

The actress – who also played the character in God of War Ragnarok – will star opposite Dave Bautista’s Kratos in the glitzy show.

The re-telling should end up feeling quite familiar, as Alastair Duncan will also return as Mimir.

Fans of the franchise will know Woll dies at the start of the story, kickstarting Kratos’ quest as he and son Atreus embark on a journey to scatter her ashes.

But we now know, during that period, Faye is trapped in a kind of afterlife for the gods known as the Everywhen. That’s where God of War Laufey will take place.

It’ll be interesting to see whether the TV show pulls in elements from the upcoming PS5 game, or if Woll’s role here will be to show Kratos’ family life prior to the events of the main game.

There’s no release date for the show just yet, but filming restarted in October with Baustita in the lead role, after previous actor Ryan Hurst was recast due to sustaining an injury on set.

Woll is an accomplished actress and knows the character inside-out, so this casting makes perfect sense to me.

#3863. Embracer begin yet another round of layoffs at Crystal Dynamics, while they're still midway through development on two Tomb Raider games

Update: Studio confirms eight staff lost their jobs

Update 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:

As initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a new set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is currently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.

This now marks the studio's fifth round of layoffs since Embracer acquired it in 2022, following cuts in March 2025, August 2025, November 2025, and March this year. This is a drastic amount even considering the current state of the industry, with layoffs seemingly happening several times a week, but unfortunately, this is par for the course for Embracer. Even still, it makes one wonder just how many staff are left at Crystal Dynamics by now. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Tomb Raider: Catalyst are still in production, so you'd hope that the studio won't be shuttered entirely.

According to Legacy of Atlantis' Steam page, generative AI has been used in the development of Legacy of Atlantis "to support some early exploration and temporary development content. Any AI-assisted assets were either replaced or refined by humans in order to maintain the creative and artistic vision of the development team." I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find new work soon.

#3862. Sony squeezes out a PlayStation 5 firmware update before the release of GTA 6

Sony has managed to squeeze out another PlayStation 5 firmware update before the highly-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Sony has been rolling firmware updates out on a fairly regular basis, and like many of those updates, this latest one - version 26.07-14.23.00 - doesn't bring any very meaningful changes. Sony repeated the same "we've made some security fixes to the system software" patch-note that we've seen many times before.

And like all those firmware updates, 26.07-14.23.00 is mandatory for all PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles, assuming you want to go online or play the latest games. That, of course, includes GTA 6, which requires the console's firmware to be updated to its latest version before you can play.

The update should download automatically the next time you turn on your console, but you can also force the download through Settings > System > System Software > System Software Update and Settings. This is also where you can tick the option for your console to automatically download and install those updates in the future.

Although Sony hasn't directly said so, the high frequency of those security firmware updates is likely related to the impending release of GTA 6, especially in light of recent gen-AI-driven PS5 jailbreaks.

Any firmware released before GTA 6's release now becomes required to play the game, which delays potential security exploits, seeing as hackers would need to find vulnerabilities in that firmware in order to play. While this may never happen, Sony is at least trying to minimise the risk as much as possible.

#3860. Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

It's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

In a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

Every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another big game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

#3857. After GTA 6's original soundtrack, Justice probably won't work on any other video game ever again

You've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and the fantastic King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, it's clear that the duo - and Rockstar - have spared no expense on the production of music for the game.

From what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City. You ought to enjoy the music while you can, though, because it seems Justice won't be coming back to video games any time soon. If ever.

Via a new interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project. "When [the offer to work with Rockstar] arrived on the table, we thought 'if there’s one video game we have to do, it's this one.' As soon as we accepted and started working [on the OST], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game."

Interesting. The duo, from the clip we can see on Rockyrama's posts, don't seem to give more information about this decision - did they have a bad time working with Rockstar? Was it intense? Or is it rather down to the fact that, if you're going to work on a game, you may as well make it what is largely expected to be the biggest game of all time.

Justice, for what it's worth, consider the work they've done on GTA 6 to be "a real album" of music - it's not seen as lesser or different to the band, just because it's being released as part of a video game. "GTA 6 gave us the excuse and direction to do it. The music always had to be listenable on its own, even if each track is tailored for [a specific] scene," the band explains.

The band's album isn't the only music connected to the game, either. There's also a 34-song album launching for the game, composed of original songs from some of the biggest artists in the world. The album features Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and many more. The full tracklist leaked at the weekend.

One unofficial GTA 6 PC port has been scrapped, hours after major progress in getting the game up and running was shown, as its lead quits and alleges that Rockstar Games has taken down the project's Discord server.

Project Leonida was one of the main GTA 6 recompilation efforts, and yesterday, as notorious leaker Cyberleek dropped an executable file for the Xbox build of the game they'd shared last week, it seemed like it wouldn't be long before the fan-made PC port was functional. The devs behind Leonida never expected things to work immediately, but mere hours after the EXE file was dropped, an update in the Discord server claimed: "The game almost boots. Black screen, audio cuts off."

In the hours that followed, it'd seem even more progress was made. One video shared on Reddit, apparently posted on the Leonida Discord server, appears to show the full opening sequence and the first-time game setup running on PC. However, don't expect any further updates from the project – or at least, not from its original creator – as the Discord server has now completely disappeared, and the project's lead says they're "stepping away" from it entirely.

"I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed writes on Twitter. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity."

In a follow-up post, they claim that Rockstar was behind the Discord server's takedown, saying: "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've said before, I'm a 15-year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle-aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye." Their original GitHub repository has also vanished, though others' clones of Leonida still appear to be live.

Even with the original version of Leonida scrapped, though, there are still other projects racing to be the first to actually work. In fact, there's a whole tracker dedicated to monitoring the progress of various projects and how close they are to being ready to work. One such project recently said: "The title boots, runs its menus at its own 30 fps and loads the world, where rendering fails."

While none are working yet, I still expect takedowns aplenty in the coming days and weeks, even if it's exceedingly difficult to completely wipe something from the internet once it's been posted.

#3855. Only two days out from GTA 6, its publisher Take-Two lay off staff at XCOM and Civilization developer Firaxis

About a third of the workforce has been cut, reportedly

Upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

Word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a company succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

Bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a new XCOM, which is yet to be announced, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development issues, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg said it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

#3854. "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before new expansion

"People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons."

Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion, Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

"For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn launched, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today."

Yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most important" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

This problem of player retention is nothing new for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is important.

Final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the new story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

The game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too, though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a new overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

#3853. Phil Spencer Might Not Be At Xbox Anymore, But He's Still Playing Loads Of Games

Phil Spencer is a legend of the Xbox division, having helped redefine the brand after a disastarous Xbox One launch in 2013, and spearheading such initiatives as Xbox Game Pass, Xbox backwards compatibility, crossplay, and a renewed focus on gaming rather than continuing the push towards "TV, TV, TV" that had proven so controversial.

It's very possible that without his influence, Xbox would have shut its doors over a decade ago.

News Microsoft Considered Pulling The Plug On Xbox Back In 2014

We haven't heard anything from Spencer since he announced his retirement earlier in 2026, but he's still very actively playing games on his Xbox consoles, including some of this year's new releases.

For example, he's racked up 940/1000 gamerscore in Echo Generation 2, 650/1000 in Forza Horizon 6, 585/1000 in Replaced, and he's also been playing the likes of Halo: Campaign Evolved, Gears of War: E-Day, Sopa - Tale of the Stolen Potato, Baldur's Gate 3, Vampire Crawlers and even Sunset Overdrive in recent months.

One of Phil's most beloved qualities as Xbox boss was that he proved himself to be a hardcore gamer, being someone who actively seeks to play games in his spare time. New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is somewhat the opposite, admitting back in February that she doesn't "pretend to be the best gamer" and that it's ultimately not her goal to be.

Anyway, Phil is busy enjoying his retirement right now, and we wish him all the best from everyone here at Pure Xbox. We unfortunately never got a chance to meet the man ourselves, but always admired his leadership from afar.

Here's hoping he might start hitting the interview circuit and doing what the likes of Peter Moore and Nintendo's Reggie Fils-Aimé have done in the past, as we'd love to see him sticking around the industry in some capacity going forward.

#3852. Today Is Your Last Chance to Play Destruction AllStars on PS5

Forgotten car combat game Destruction AllStars has been in some stage of extinction for years now, but if you do have the PS5 game in your library, then today truly is the last day you can play it in any meaningful manner.

From tomorrow, 25th November 2026, the last of its game services will be taken offline.

The multiplayer servers were already permanently pulled in May 2026, and within the next 24 hours, "all remaining game services will be taken offline", per communication from Sony.

Single player modes had still been available to play, but those will be removed too when their servers are taken offline.

Quite literally the only content left in Destruction AllStars after tomorrow is an arcade mode and challenges. Even then, though, Sony warns the "functionality and player experience" tied to that content could be impacted.

Basically, if you want to experience even a sliver of the Destruction AllStars experience, you've only got today left to do it. It's already been delisted from the PS Store, so if you don't have a copy now, you're completely out of luck.

It's not like you'd be missing out on much, to be fair.

Destruction AllStars never made a splash in terms of quality or popularity. While it did have a small playerbase during its days with active servers, the game quickly died out after a February 2021 release.

Will you be playing Destruction AllStars one last time today? Let us know in the comments below.

[source News: PS5's Destruction AllStars Delisted and Disabled Without Notice Due to 'Ongoing Technical Issues']

#3851. Is it time to retire Dragon Quest as a series? Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it might be

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something new. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

"The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," said Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)"

Horii himself seems undeterred: with the new mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

"What's important is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people."

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the company aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

#3850. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

"We ended up just cutting and cutting it."

It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross New York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far."

The pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something new," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty quickly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died."

The increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The big project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again."

Rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA."

Agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished."

While never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij said. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched."

As for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij said, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

Needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them."

According to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

One thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

"I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

"At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!"

We could be saying goodbye to Bucky Barnes in Avengers: Doomsday

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Avengers: Doomsday is fast approaching, and everyone seems pretty convinced Bucky Barnes isn't making it out alive.

Sebastian Stan has a role in The Batman 2, which set off alarm bells for Marvel fans that the Winter Soldier might not be returning for more in the MCU – and now an update from Stan himself only seems to seal the deal.

"I'm always happy to keep playing him. I don't know if the decision's up to me, ultimately," Stan said on the Next Best Picture podcast.

When prompted by the interviewer that he must have some sway, Stan said: "Well, I don't know, to be honest with you. I'm ready to take the character in all kinds of different ways, but I can't make that decision, it's the powers that be. And I think they have a lot going on, they have a lot on their plate. Do I feel we've explored that character, there's nowhere else to go, I think we did our best? I do think we've done our best so far.

"I don't think that that character totally got to fully live out his arc in the way that he has in the comics for instance, or that I've wanted," he continued. "I've been a big fan of the whole Black Widow of it all. But that's not the only way, you could take him in all kinds of ways. I've spoken about this Sicario-esque paranoid thriller where he just recognizes this person on the street and thinks it's a torturer from Hydra, like back in the day, and he becomes obsessed and starts following the person and realizes the person has a family. And then he's like, 'Am I crazy or is this the guy…?' and confronts the person, the guy denies it.

"Kevin just sort of went, "Sounds good, uh, we'll see,'" he added with a laugh. "So, I'm always ready, but we're at that point now where I can feel it, he needs to either evolve somewhere, or maybe it's time. It's one of those."

Now, while it sounds like Stan still has tons of ideas when it comes to Bucky Barnes, it also certainly sounds like he's made peace with leaving the character behind. We'll find out when Avengers: Doomsday finally arrives on December 18.

In the meantime, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV shows for everything else the MCU has in store.

#3848. Guide: GTA 6: Vice City Easter Egg Walkthrough & Tommy Vercetti Shirt Unlock

Find the portal and get your Tommy Vercetti rewards

GTA 6 is hiding an extremely cool Easter egg related to 2002's GTA: Vice City. While it's a really fun reward and absolutely worth looking for, it involves quite a complex set of steps to make it happen. In this GTA 6 guide, we're going to explain how to find the Vice City Easter egg.

Full credit to Memeio for discovering this secret!

On this page: GTA 6: Vice City Easter Egg Walkthrough & Tommy Vercetti Shirt Unlock

Below is a full walkthrough of how to do the Vice City Easter egg in GTA 6 and get the Tommy Vercetti rewards. Follow these steps and you can find the Vice City Easter egg for yourself.

Note: Because this is a walkthrough of the whole process, you may find spoilers below.

Your first stop is the Badger R&D radio tower in Key Lento, not far from Jason's home. Here it is on the map for reference:

Go to the tower and climb it, walking up the internal stairs and then climbing the ladders to reach the top:

In this room, there's an electrical box on the wall with a lever you can pull; set the lever to the upper 'ON' position:

On the opposite side of the room, push the button on the equipment:

You should hear a sound effect play (taken directly from GTA: Vice City).

On the back wall are a couple of posters that provide some clues as to what you need to do. First is a poster for LPL, the power company in GTA 6. The second advertises the JoySystem bearing the phrase, "Lose Track of Time":

"Lose Track of Time" is a reference to "Life Is Passing Me By", which is a well-known cheat code in GTA: Vice City that speeds up the in-game clock.

Your goal now is to visit 12 substations all across Leonida in a particular order. When you reach each one, you will need to press certain buttons, slowly entering the old school cheat code.

Note: You cannot fast travel to these locations, you must reach them all manually. Also, some of these substations are staffed and you will be trespassing while you're on the premises, so be careful.

Let's go through each stop on your substation tour:

The first substation is in Vice City's Downtown district. Here's its location on the map:

Look left to see a building with an 'L' by the door:

Go inside and find the machine with a label on it that reads "Press D" — push that button:

Substation #2 is located in the Balsero district. Here it is on the map:

Hop the fence and go inside the door next to the letters 'iF':

In the room inside, turn left and approach the machine with the label 'Press D' and push the button:

Substation #3 is back in Key Lento. Here it is on the map:

Hop the fence and make your way to the main building. You're looking for a door next to the letters 'Ei' on the wall:

Go inside; just to the right is a machine with the label 'Press •'. Push the button:

Substation #4 is located on Penmarch Isle in the Washington Beach region. Here's where you'll find it:

And here's a slightly more zoomed out view:

When you reach it, hop over the fence and look for this small hut with an 'S' by the door:

Just inside on the left is a machine; push the button labeled 'Press A':

Substation #5 is found in Vice City, in the Crosstown district. Here it is on the map:

Get over the fence and go around the side of the building — you will find a 'P' on the wall:

There are a series of boxes on the wall here; you need to pull the lever marked 'Press •':

Substation #6 is found in Port Gellhorn. Here it is on the map:

Over the fence, look right to find a building with an 'A' on the wall:

Here, there are several levers you can pull. Pull the one marked 'Press A':

Substation #7 is found in Hamlet, as shown on the map:

Find the building with 'Ss' on the side. If you go during the day, there will be staff outside it:

Inside, press the button labeled 'Press A':

Substation #8 is within a large facility in Gloriana Key. Here's where it is on the map:

Inside, find the button labeled 'Press A', and push it:

Return to Hamlet for Substation #9. Here it is on the map:

Hop the fence and find the building with a 'G' on its wall:

Head around to the back of the building and find the lever marked 'Press •'. Pull it:

Substation #10 is right at the very bottom of Port Gellhorn, as shown on the map:

Approach the building with the 'Me' on the wall:

Just below these letters is the lever you need to pull, labeled 'Press W':

Substation #11 is once again back in Hamlet. Here's its spot on the map:

Find the small building with a 'B' on the wall:

Last but not least, Substation #12 is found in North Mariana County, as shown on the map:

Find the small building with the 'Y' on its wall:

Next to that letter is a lever marked 'Press W' — pull it:

If you've visited all the above substations in the correct order and pressed/pulled all the correct buttons and levers, you will receive a strange text message that reads as follows:

What you need to do is travel to the T.H. Power Station between the in-game hours of 7pm and 6am. Here it is on the map:

This area is heavily guarded so be careful getting into the power station. Make your way to Reactor 2, where you will see a very obvious portal:

Next to the portal is a lever — pull it and you'll be transported into GTA: Vice City, complete with pixelated visuals:

When you leave, you'll receive a couple of special items as a reward!

Once you've completed the Easter egg, you'll be back in regular ol' GTA 6 with two very cool items for your trouble.

First, you get Tommy Vercetti's iconic blue Hawaiian shirt:

Second is the 'American Glory' motorcycle:

Important Note: You will need to register the American Glory motorcycle at a Pay ‘n’ Spray or park it in one of your garages to ensure you keep the bike across sessions.

Yes, after you go through the portal and unlock the Easter egg's rewards, both Jason and Lucia will be able to wear a Tommy Vercetti-inspired shirt and use the motorcycle.

The Vice City Easter egg in GTA 6 can take quite a long time to complete, because you have to drive all over the map and ensure you're at the right places and pushing the right buttons.

However, yes, it's ultimately worth the effort because you get to see something truly unique, plus you get some really cool, unique items that GTA fans will love.

And that's how to find the Vice City Easter egg in GTA 6. Have you found it and picked up your rewards yet? Tell us in the comments section below, and check out our GTA 6 guide for more.

#3847. Call of Duty might have swapped guns and tanks for knights and swords if an Infinity Ward experiment had panned out

"If it's a war story, sure, it can be COD."

As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold new directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

This latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty."

This isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

As for Kurosaki, he currently leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

#3846. Archetype go all in on the Mass Effect vibes with a FemJun reveal, but I'm just left hoping they'll call the alternative option MascJun to balance it out

I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

"Fortnite also took a hit," though not quite as hard

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

As GTA 6 continues to celebrate its unparalleled launch, other games are falling behind Rockstar's behemoth in popularity, analysts report – including generally high-population online titles, such as Call of Duty… and even Fortnite.

Rhys Elliott, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, reveals as much in a new post over on X, writing that "GTA 6's launch hit Call of Duty HARD, Alinea Analytics estimates." So, how hard are we talking?"CoD HQ's daily active users across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam are down 42% from an average of 7.5 million DAUs to 4.4 million." That's nearly 50% – and when you narrow things down to PlayStation, Call of Duty's "main platform," it's worse.

On Sony's consoles, "Call of Duty took a 44% hit," as Elliott writes. "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline." We're now on day five, and something tells me it's not much better. It isn't just Call of Duty, which recently released Modern Warfare 4, either. "Fortnite also took a hit, with its DAUs on PlayStation and Xbox paragliding down 28% from 17.8 million to 12.8 million."

Unlike Call of Duty, though, Fortnite has seen a bit of a recovery. As Elliott puts it, "Fortnite very much has its hooks in its player base, so it already managed to claw back some folks (back to 19% below its baseline) by the end of the weekend." Not to mention that "Fortnite is holding one of its big live events to tie up the current season on Dec 5," which the analyst says "Epic hopes will pull players back after they've polished off GTA 6's story."

What really stands out here is that GTA 6 currently only has a story mode. There's no online counterpart like the one many know and love Grand Theft Auto 5 for – and it's tough to imagine what the future of other online games (like, you know, Call of Duty and Fornite) will look like then. "When the online component and PC port of GTA 6 land," as Elliott himself speculates, "it's going to be rough times for these live-service titles."

Indeed, it will be – or so I believe, anyway. Only time will tell for certain, and there's no knowing when the online mode will even drop as it stands now… that and the PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6, which we've heard zilch about.

The next season of content is coming soon to Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve's online multiplayer mode.

Publisher Bandai Namco has released the below trailer detailing all the new bits and bobs:

Season 2 of Ace Combat Online begins on 1st December, 2026, and there's plenty of new stuff for frequent flyers to enjoy.

#3843. Mondrayn is a putrid, crunchy pixel art RPG about escaping from limbo where "dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering"

Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

#3842. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is the US' best-selling physical game so far this year

The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

Ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

Lego Jeff the Land Shark has been officially revealed, and the kit will be hitting shelves on January 1. You can check it out for yourself at the Lego store, though it's not up for pre-order quite yet.

The most precious boy from Marvel Rivals is apparently getting a Lego set if leaks are to be believed, but fans are seriously divided on how Lego Jeff the Land Shark looks.

Popping up via reliable source Unibricks on Instagram, Lego Jeff the Land Shark looks to be a mid-size figure that's roughly on par with Lego Eevee. Much like his inspiration from Marvel Rivals and the comics, he's all toothy grins, big cartoon eyes, and stubby little legs… but the result has received mixed reactions from fans who aren't entirely sold on the idea. The comments on Unibrick's post trend toward the negative, while responses on a Reddit post sharing a video of the set from New Elementary are split down the middle – they basically veer from "aw, so cute!" to "oh man, that's hideous."

Want more Jeff in your life? There's plenty of merch based on his appearance in Marvel Rivals, from tees to action figures. You can find it all at Amazon, where a lot is getting a discount ahead of Black Friday.

I understand this mixed reception. While the alleged model does capture that signature smile and happy-go-lucky vibe, it doesn't quite replicate Jeff's squishy, rotund look. The tail on this leaked set feels a little sparse too, as if it's missing pieces. (I assume this is so the fin can 'wag' thanks to a ball joint, but it looks odd at a glance.)

Still, I think the team's done the best they can with the scale they're working at – and I'm not sure I'd call it 'bad' by any means. Soft and rounded characters are really hard to recreate in Lego brick form at this size due to the toy's angular nature. While a few of the best Lego sets manage it through some eldritch sorcery (Munchlax or Wallace & Gromit come to mind), I can only imagine how tricky it is with a shark that is basically a spongy football with legs.

There's no word on when this kit would launch, but if it's January, that month is looking very busy - a host of Marvel kits are also hitting the Lego store then.

Either way, this leaked kit is just one of many Jeff-themed pieces of merch coming out; although the recent Hasbro Marvel Rivals action figures are cool, I only have eyes for the Jeff the Land Shark action figure.

#3840. The siren call of user-generated content has caught Dead by Daylight in its snare, as Behaviour Interactive outline a big revamp update slated for next year

Weather, new models, better maps, it'll have it all

The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

"What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely new modes, the possibilities are vast."

The post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial."

Beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

#3839. Sci-fi RPG Exodus continues evoking Mass Effect by revealing female lead and nicknaming her FemJun

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

There are, however, big and important differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

Archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons company Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Archetype announced a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

Matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year."

Didn't you hear? You can't even steal cars anymore.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you ever watch science videos on social media, you've probably been served a video of someone debunking the claims of a flat earther.

It starts with a clip of some belligerent dope demanding to know why, if the earth is so round, ships don't disappear over the horizon. A greenscreened science communicator then appears, rubs their forehead, and shows us a video of a ship disappearing over the horizon. Checkmate.

It's good content, but if you linger too long on one of those videos, you'll get another, and then another, and pretty soon your whole feed will be debunking videos. Now you're enrolled in a never ending lesson plan which features such insights as 'an all-meat diet is not good for you,' 'the moon landing was real,' and 'hating women is not in fact based.'

The total effect of this is that the most ignorant and dishonest quacks and provocateurs get to set the level of discourse, and instead of investigating new metaphorical horizons in topics that interest you, you wind up watching people debate the existence of the actual horizon.

Which brings me to Grand Theft Auto 6. Despite making $3.79 billion on its launch day, it's easy to stumble across confident social media claims that it's a total flop and everyone's going to refund it. According to popular X posts, GTA 6 doesn't even let you steal cars anymore, and there are hundreds of Metacritic user reviewers insisting that it's far-left propaganda rather than the mass-market entertainment product it obviously is.

It's the videogame discourse version of flat eartherism. The millions of people playing GTA 6 do not think it is a "cuck simulator" because you can buy a woman flowers, but it's hard not to react to the few dorks making that claim, even though focusing on debunking them severely limits the depth of the conversations we can then have about the game. Good luck discussing your feelings if you dislike GTA 6 for normal reasons!

Over the past few days, I've entertained sparks of hope that GTA 6 could be the flashpoint that brings us out of this era of videogame discourse. The millions of people playing it and not reacting like buffoons are surely irrefutable evidence that culture war dunces don't represent the masses.

But then again, we're still pointing at videos of ships going over the horizon to prove that the earth isn't flat.

#3836. PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

12.2 million gamers can be wrong, apparently.

Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation users claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

The case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

The lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the company.
